review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read Mathlib's SchwartzMap Fourier section, `Real.fourier_eq`, and the other uses of `fourier_postcompCLM` and `isWeakDivFree_congr_ae` in the library. The one justified generalisation is `fourier_postcompCLM`, whose proof never uses anything specific to `L2Vec3`. The other statements (the gradient-of-covector bound, the Leray and Stokes range results, the weak-divergence congruence) are tied to the 3D Hilbert setting by design, and I found no useful generalisation for them. I could not run Lean. The generalised proof is believed to go through unchanged because it only uses `Real.fourier_eq`, `f.integrable` and `ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm`, which all hold for a general finite-dimensional real inner product space `V` with `[MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V]`. That is untested.

findings.excerpt:
(L : F →L[ℂ] G) (f : SchwartzMap L2Vec3 F) :
    𝓕 (f.postcompCLM L) = (𝓕 f).postcompCLM L
findings.problem: The lemma is stated only for Schwartz maps on the specific space `L2Vec3`. The proof uses nothing about that space. It only needs the Fourier integral formula `Real.fourier_eq`, integrability of Schwartz maps, and `ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm`. Mathlib builds the Schwartz-space Fourier transform on any real inner product space `V` that is finite-dimensional and has `[MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V]`, so the lemma is needlessly specialised. It is also a generic fact about Schwartz maps that Mathlib lacks, and its name suggests a general result.
findings.proposed_change: Replace `L2Vec3` by a variable `{V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V]`. The statement becomes `theorem fourier_postcompCLM {V F G : Type*} ... (L : F →L[ℂ] G) (f : SchwartzMap V F) : 𝓕 (f.postcompCLM L) = (𝓕 f).postcompCLM L`. Keep the proof, replacing `L2Vec3` by `V` in the `change` and `calc` lines. Existing uses at `L2Vec3` unify with the general statement by instance resolution, so no call site changes. This depends on the usual `MeasureSpace V` instance for finite-dimensional inner product spaces, as in the Mathlib Schwartz Fourier section.
findings.benefit: The lemma becomes reusable for Schwartz maps on any finite-dimensional inner product space. It could be upstreamed next to `SchwartzMap.fourier_fderivCLM_eq`. It also removes a misleading dependence on the `L2Vec3` model, and every existing use keeps working.
